items.title: Not Good: Medicare Proposes $107 Billion in Bonus Cuts. That’s a Big Risk for UnitedHealth and Humana
items.summary: Key TakeawaysUnitedHealth fell 1% today after CMS proposed star-ratings changes it estimates would cut Medicare Advantage bonuses by about $107 billion between 2031 and 2037. Humana has the most at stake, because its expected earnings rebound in 2027 depends on recovering from this year’s star-ratings hit.

items.title: Health Insurers Stocks Slide Again on Latest Medicare Proposal
items.summary: Shares of US health insurers including UnitedHealth Group Inc. fell sharply in early trading Monday after federal health officials proposed changes to the Medicare program poised to cut billions in payments to insurers in the years ahead.

items.title: UnitedHealth, Humana and CVS Shares Fall as Medicare Advantage Rating Changes Threaten $107 Billion in Payments
items.summary: Shares of major US health insurance companies declined sharply in premarket trading after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed changes to its Medicare Advantage Star Ratings programme that could reduce industry payments by approximately $107 billion over a ten-year period. UnitedHealth Group (NYSE:UNH) fell 6.

items.title: Health insurer stocks slide as Medicare Advantage proposal threatens payments
items.summary: Investing.com -- Shares of major health insurers fell in premarket trading today after the U.S. government proposed changes to Medicare Advantage quality ratings that analysts warned could substantially reduce future payments to the industry.
